title: plugin-security: pin the authored-policy outcome and the skipped sharing relief on a controlled_by_parent predicate write (after #36282)
body:
repo:objectstack#4 · os-project-manager · session_01FEkQ5kt9AD1TPLy7Y9oa9D

Filing gate: ② follow-up from a landing PR (PR #36282, card #35802). It carries nit N3 of contract record 7076369115 (seat 7, PASS at `4fe236dbd1`). Maintainer 2026-11-22 07:49Z 「你后续的小改动可以另立卡。尽快完成合并」. Source: fleet. ⛔ Not a claim. Queued, not dispatched by area a4-E.

## Why

PR #36282 declares a breaking outcome: on a `controlled_by_parent` detail with an app-authored `update`/`delete` row-level policy, a non-delegated predicate write is now bounded by that policy alone. The outcome has no pin of its own on the vouched path. The skipped sharing relief on a vouched write has none either.

Both run through code the by-id path shares, and the flipped pin asserts that the composed predicate carries no floor. So this card is coverage, not a known defect.

## Done when

- **Authored-policy case.** A real-engine case in `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/predicate-write-floor-deferral.test.ts`, or a sibling file, sets up:
  - a `controlled_by_parent` detail;
  - an authored `update` policy with a `using`;
  - a caller who created rows that the policy does not admit.

  The case shows that a predicate update writes exactly the rows a by-id update of each would, and that it skips the caller's own rows the policy does not admit. Do the same for `delete`.
- **Sharing relief.** A case shows that a vouched predicate write asks no sharing verdict, or shows why none is observable.
- **Ablations.** Each case is ablated red, then restored.

Land after PR #36282.
